boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Lafayette traditions spanning first-year milestones, senior rituals, service, song, rivalry, recognition, and campus celebrations.

cards.title: Count Down from 1,000
cards.subtitle: A first-year formal marks roughly 1,000 nights until graduation
cards.notes: Watch first-year announcements in early fall, then register and bring formal attire; guests and upperclass students are not admitted.
cards.short_summary: First-years begin their Lafayette countdown with a class-only formal and dancing.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette says 1,000 Nights has been a student tradition for 30 years and marks 1,000 nights until graduation with a first-year formal.
cards.source_title: Class of 2029: Save the date for 1,000 Nights!
cards.access_notes: Registration is required. The documented 2025 event admitted first-year students only; guests and upperclass students were not permitted.

cards.title: Paint the Campus Maroon
cards.subtitle: A full week builds toward the Lafayette–Lehigh football game
cards.notes: Follow the annual schedule for banner making, performances, Quad Lighting, and the game; individual activities may require registration.
cards.short_summary: The historic football matchup expands into banners, lights, performances, and campus-wide spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette describes the Lafayette–Lehigh matchup as one of its most beloved traditions and documented a 2025 week of banner making, Quad Lighting, and community activities.
cards.source_title: The community spirit of Rivalry Week
cards.access_notes: Activity access varies by the annual schedule. A separate ticket may be necessary for the football game.

cards.title: Turn One Day into Service
cards.subtitle: Lafayette’s National Day of Service connects campus and alumni volunteers
cards.notes: Check the annual service listings, choose a posted community project, and follow its registration, transportation, and clothing guidance.
cards.short_summary: Students, employees, and alumni volunteer through one Lafayette-wide day of community projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette identifies Lafapalooza as its annual National Day of Service, when students, faculty, staff, and alumni serve communities.
cards.access_notes: Project locations and participation requirements change by year; consult Lafayette’s current service announcement before attending.

cards.title: Sing Where the Alma Mater Says
cards.subtitle: Alumni gather on Pardee Hall’s steps during Reunion Weekend
cards.notes: Join only during an announced college gathering, bring the published lyrics, and leave candles or other materials to event organizers.
cards.short_summary: The alma mater becomes literal when Lafayette voices gather in front of Old Pardee.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette documents the longstanding tradition of singing the alma mater on Old Pardee’s steps and says the Reunion Weekend singalong continues today.
cards.access_notes: The documented performance occurs as part of Reunion programming; consult the current Reunion schedule for eligibility and timing.

cards.title: Choose the Lafayette Ideal
cards.subtitle: The campus community helps recognize one graduating senior
cards.notes: Nominate an eligible senior or vote during the published spring window; review the official criteria before submitting a selection.
cards.short_summary: An annual campus vote translates Lafayette’s broad ideal into recognition for one senior.
cards.evidence_claim: Established in 1923, the George Wharton Pepper Prize is awarded annually to the senior who most nearly represents the Lafayette ideal, with campus nominations and voting.
cards.access_notes: Applications, nominations, and voting are limited to the eligibility groups and dates published by Lafayette each year.

cards.title: Give a Professor the Last Word
cards.subtitle: Graduating seniors select a professor for one final class address
cards.notes: Graduating seniors should watch for nominations and the final event notice, then confirm the room and any RSVP requirement before attending.
cards.short_summary: The graduating class chooses a professor to close its Lafayette education with parting wisdom.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette’s 2025 Last Lecture featured a professor selected by the graduating class, and the official calendar described it as a recurring favorite among graduates.
cards.access_notes: The documented event was intended for the Class of 2025. Future attendance rules, venue, and time require the current event listing.

cards.title: Hold the Marquis’ Sword
cards.subtitle: Pepper Prize finalists receive cords beside a treasured artifact
cards.notes: Pepper Prize finalists should follow Advising instructions for the ceremony; others can view the college’s official photo documentation.
cards.short_summary: Finalists share recognition through ceremonial cords and Lafayette’s historic sword.
cards.evidence_claim: At the annual 2026 Cord and Sword Ceremony, Pepper Prize finalists received cords and held the Marquis de Lafayette’s sword as part of a documented spring tradition.
cards.access_notes: Ceremonial participation is for Pepper Prize finalists; the source does not establish general public attendance.

cards.title: Dress Up for the Final 100 Hours
cards.subtitle: A senior-only formal closes the Lafayette countdown
cards.notes: Graduating seniors should register before the firm deadline, purchase a nontransferable ticket, and use college-provided transportation.
cards.short_summary: The senior class reunites at a formal held near the final hours before Commencement.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette called its 2025 event the 43rd annual 100 Hours formal and limited attendance to graduating Lafayette seniors with advance registration and ticket purchase.
cards.source_title: Senior Corner: Events, to-dos, and number of days until Commencement 2025
cards.access_notes: The documented 2025 formal was restricted to Lafayette seniors; guests and underclass students were excluded, and advance registration was mandatory.

cards.title: Wait for the Quad to Glow
cards.subtitle: Rivalry Week opens Lafayette’s winter season with campus lights
cards.notes: Meet on the Quad at the announced start time, dress for November weather, and check the event notice if you need parking guidance.
cards.short_summary: Lights, student performances, crafts, and warm drinks transform the Quad during Rivalry Week.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette calls Quad Lighting an annual college tradition and documented the 2025 gathering with lights, hot beverages, crafts, and performances.
cards.source_title: Join the College’s annual Quad Lighting
cards.access_notes: The event date changes annually. Use Lafayette’s current Rivalry Week or campus-event notice for timing and weather updates.

cards.title: Watch the Free Bridge Turn Maroon
cards.subtitle: Easton’s historic span glows in Lafayette’s color for Commencement
cards.notes: View the programmed LEDs from a lawful public riverfront or bridge approach; confirm the current lighting date before making the trip.
cards.short_summary: A Lafayette-designed Easton landmark joins Commencement by glowing maroon across the Delaware.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette Magazine reports that lighting the historic Northampton Street Bridge for Commencement began as a new tradition in 2024.
cards.access_notes: Lighting is externally programmed and date-specific; observe only from open public areas and verify the current Commencement schedule.

warnings: Event dates, eligibility, registration, and ticket terms can change annually; cards distinguish documented editions from standing traditions.
No coordinates or map URLs were included because exact event positions or official map links were not verified from the cited evidence pages.
